description:
WHEN 0 at :222 taken together with the TRUE side of the plaintext password comparison at :223 - the first of the three ordered arms of EVALUATE WS-RESP-CD at :221-257 - reached by a key the file holds, and used here to isolate the password normalisation at :135-136 from the user-id normalisation at :132-134. The user id is typed in upper case, so :132-134 is an identity move and cannot be what makes this case pass; only the password is typed in lower case, so the sign-on depends entirely on :135-136. A translation that normalised the key and forgot the password would still pass case02, case03, case09 and case10 - which all normalise both fields or neither - and would fail exactly here and nowhere else. That is the whole purpose of this slot, and it is why the typed pair is USER0003 with a lower-case password rather than any other combination.

In source order: EVALUATE TRUE at :117-130 falls through to WHEN OTHER CONTINUE at :128-129 because neither field is blank; :132-136 upper-cases the id into WS-USER-ID and CDEMO-USER-ID and the password into WS-USER-PWD; :138 finds NOT ERR-FLG-ON and performs READ-USER-SEC-FILE; the EXEC CICS READ at :211-219 addresses row eight on the key USER0003 and reports DFHRESP(NORMAL), which common/FileStatus.java names NORMAL and fixes at the raw literal 0 - the value :222 evaluates against - and which FileStatus.fromCicsResp maps onto FileStatus.Outcome.OK; :223 then compares SEC-USR-PWD against WS-USER-PWD, eight characters against eight, and they are equal precisely because :135-136 has already normalised the typed value. WS-ERR-FLG is never touched on this path and remains at the SET ERR-FLG-OFF of :75, so it reads 'N'; the contrast is the not-found arm at :248 and the unexpected-response arm at :253, both of which move 'Y' into it, while the wrong-password ELSE at :241-246 leaves it alone as case14 pins in detail.

forcedOutcomes is empty because nothing needs forcing: the key is one of the ten actually seeded, so the found arm is reached from the data itself. Only case11 forces an outcome, and only because its WHEN OTHER at :252-256 is unreachable from any arrangement of rows - a closed file, an invalid request or a length error, none of which a seeded dataset can produce.

The exit is a transfer, and every part of that is asserted. :227 moves SEC-USR-TYPE into CDEMO-USER-TYPE, the row's type is 'U' at offset 56, so CDEMO-USRTYP-ADMIN at :230 is false and control takes the ELSE at :235-239 rather than the admin branch at :231-234. nextProgram is therefore the regular-user target named by the literal at :237, the response names no mapset and no map, sends is empty because :231-239 hands the client a program name rather than a screen, and cursorField is absent because :230-240 contains no MOVE -1 anywhere. termination is XCTL, and the EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID at :98-102 is never executed on this path because XCTL does not come back. SignOnService enforces the same equivalence from the other side - a successful sign-on is an XCTL and nothing else, and only an XCTL names a target - so a response that painted a screen here, or that signed on without naming a program, would be refused before it could ever be compared. This case is one of the seven of the twenty that sign on, and one of the two that reach the regular-user target, so both arms of :230 are driven across the set and neither target is assumed.

The communication area is where the statelessness is asserted. Five of the sixteen CARDDEMO-COMMAREA fields of app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:19-44 are written on this path and only on this path: :224 moves WS-TRANID into CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, giving CC00; :225 moves WS-PGMNAME into CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM, giving COSGN00C; :226 moves the normalised WS-USER-ID into CDEMO-USER-ID, giving USER0003 in upper case although a lower-case password was typed; :227 moves the record's SEC-USR-TYPE into CDEMO-USER-TYPE, giving 'U'; and :228 moves ZEROS into CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT. Note that CDEMO-USER-ID is written twice on a successful sign-on, unconditionally at :134 and again at :226, and both moves carry the same normalised value, so the field is not evidence of which statement wrote it. The remaining eleven fields pass through untouched and are pinned as such. The area arrives blank, which is the faithful state for a sign-on: no customer has been selected, no account opened and no card chosen, so the customer identifier and the three names, the account identifier and status, the card number and the last map and mapset are all still empty when the transfer is handed over. A translation holding any of this in a session rather than carrying it in the payload would have nothing to hand to the program named by :237.

USRSEC is seeded from app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44, whose ten in-stream rows are 57 characters where app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23 declares 80: SEC-USR-ID X(08) at 0, SEC-USR-FNAME X(20) at 8, SEC-USR-LNAME X(20) at 28, SEC-USR-PWD X(08) at 48, SEC-USR-TYPE X(01) at 56 - which is 57 - then SEC-USR-FILLER X(23) at 57, which is 80. The 23-byte shortfall is supplied once at seed time by the declared USRSEC_FILLER_PAD_57_TO_80 normalisation and is never hand-padded into the rows. The same job corroborates the target width twice, with DCB=(LRECL=80,RECFM=FB) on SYSUT2 and RECORDSIZE(80,80) KEYS(8,0) on the cluster it loads; KEYS(8,0) is also why the eight-character key built at :215-216 addresses the whole of SEC-USR-ID and nothing beyond it.

Row eight - rowIndex 7, the row the typed key addresses - is pinned twice over: by all six named fields, so the comparison at :223 is diffed field for field rather than as one opaque string, and by the complete 80-character image, so the total width is asserted too and a record that omitted SEC-USR-FILLER would be short by exactly 23. The record was read and it matched, so its decoded field set belongs to the observation; that is the same rule case14 applies to a record that was read and did not match, and the opposite of a not-found path, where there is no record and therefore no field set to pin. SEC-USR-PWD is pinned as the stored PASSWORD in upper case while the request typed it in lower case, which is the byte-level statement of what this case exists to prove. The other nine rows are pinned by image alone, and the dataset-level expectation adds the row count and the record width on top, so a dataset that lost or gained a row is caught even where no row-level expectation would notice.

expectedWrites is empty as a positive assertion: COSGN00C contains no WRITE, REWRITE or DELETE on any path, and the read at :211-219 does not specify UPDATE, so it takes no lock and holds no record. The ten expectedFinalState images therefore also assert that a successful sign-on leaves the security file exactly as it found it - no last-logon stamp, no counter, no audit row, none of which the COBOL writes and none of which may be added. The dataset is addressed by its binding key USRSEC - the CICS file name at :39 and the FILE definition in app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD - and never by a dataset name. expectedReturnCode is 0 because grep -c RETURN-CODE over the program is 0.

expectedMessages is empty and sends is empty, and the two together say something specific: this path emits nothing at all. app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl contains no DISPLAY anywhere, so there is no line to record; and because SEND-SIGNON-SCREEN at :145-157 is not performed, POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :177-204 is never reached either. One consequence is worth stating rather than leaving to be inferred: the MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE at :179 does not execute on this path, so no header is painted and none of TRNNAMEO, TITLE01O, CURDATEO, PGMNAMEO, TITLE02O, CURTIMEO, APPLIDO, SYSIDO, USERIDO, PASSWDO or ERRMSGO is produced. The clock is still pinned at 2022-07-19T23:12:33 - traceable to this program's own version footer at :259 and expressed as a fixed local date-time so no timezone can shift it - because a case must be deterministic whether or not the value is read, and because a translation that painted a screen here would then be caught against a known instant rather than against whatever the wall clock happened to say. For the same reason the two EXEC CICS ASSIGN calls at :198-204 are not reached, so the CICSAWS1 and AWS1 constants the painting cases substitute for them do not arise here. The charset is named US-ASCII explicitly, because the ASCII fixtures are US-ASCII and the platform default is never relied on.

Two deviations recorded rather than quietly worked around. First, app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl:59 is *COPY DFHATTR. with the asterisk in column 7, which makes it a COBOL comment, so no DFHATTR attribute constant applies to this program however many other programs copy that member. Second, COSGN00C never copies CSSETATY - its only consumer is COACTUPC - so there is no DFHRED plus '*' highlight applied at run time and no xxxC, xxxP, xxxH or xxxV item is assigned anywhere; on this path the question does not even arise, since no map is sent and there is consequently no attribute metadata of any kind to record. Where a run-time attribute value would come from is common/BmsAttributes, which reproduces DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR from IBM CICS documentation because both are IBM-supplied and absent from this checkout, as DFHAID is too - which is also why the attention identifier is named here by its common/CicsAid mnemonic DFHENTER and never as a raw byte.

The security posture is unchanged in both directions, and this case drives the positive side of it. :223 compares SEC-USR-PWD against WS-USER-PWD in plaintext, and the ten seeded rows keep that legacy plaintext span byte for byte, because digesting the stored value would reject every seeded row and change which requests sign on. Nothing is interposed on either side of the comparison: no credential store, no digest, no issued session credential and no security filter chain appears anywhere in this case, and the lower-case password is accepted only because :135-136 normalised it and not because any tolerance was added to the comparison itself - case17 holds that same comparison to a single differing character and is refused. The plaintext credential is an inherited property of the legacy design and an explicit non-goal of this migration, recorded here so that it stays visible rather than buried, not because it is endorsed.

Provenance. Every expected value above is statically derived - by structured reading of app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl cross-checked against app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy for the record layout, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy for the communication area, app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy for the two titles, whose line 21 is commented out so that line 22 is the active CCDA-TITLE02, app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy for the header, app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY with app/bms/COSGN00.bms for the screen field shapes, app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD for transaction CC00 and the USRSEC file, and app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44 for the ten seed rows. It was never captured from a live COBOL execution, which is empirically impossible in this environment: there is no z/OS or CICS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled, no Language Environment CEE* services exist, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR are absent from the repository. Only the provenance of the expected values is substituted; the twenty cases, the field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-equals-zero gate all stand, and the substitution is escalated rather than absorbed.

The unit is SignOnService, driven as a plain object with a fixture-backed SecUserRepository - no MockMvc, no HTTP, no servlet container and no JobLauncher in the path. Exactly one keyed read is performed, the one at :211-219, and it addresses row eight. All conversation state travels in the payload, so no server-side session exists to hold any of it. Neither the backward-GO TO restructuring gate nor the CEE3ABD gate applies: grep -c 'GO TO' and grep -c CEE3ABD over app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl are both 0, and neither is faked. DUPKEY, DUPREC and ENDFILE are unreachable from this program, whose only file operation is that single keyed READ, so none of them is fabricated here; of the three outcomes this program can reach, this case is the found one.
